details: On Monday, July 20, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) kept its one-year Loan Prime Rate (LPR) at 3.00% and the five-year LPR at 3.50% for the 14th consecutive month. This decision was largely in line with market expectations, reflecting a cautious stance by policymakers who are balancing support for an uneven economic recovery with currency stability, despite softer-than-expected second-quarter economic data.
title: China Maintains Key Lending Rates Amid Economic Slowdown

details: Oil prices surged on July 20, with Brent crude surpassing $90 per barrel, as the conflict between the United States and Iran intensified. The escalating hostilities have raised concerns over crude supplies from the Middle East and disrupted shipping through the vital Strait of Hormuz. This geopolitical tension is contributing to risk aversion and pushing up US gas prices, fueling broader inflationary pressures.
title: US-Iran Tensions Push Oil Above $90, Fueling Inflation Fears

details: The Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act), enacted in July 2025, reached its July 2026 deadline for implementing regulations. On July 20, updates included proposed reporting forms and instructions for FDIC-supervised permitted payment stablecoin issuers. America's Credit Unions provided feedback on NCUA's proposal, advocating for clarity and risk-based assessments. This legislation aims to create a comprehensive regulatory framework for fiat-backed stablecoins.
title: US Advances Stablecoin Regulations Under GENIUS Act

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) is widely anticipated to keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting on July 23, following a 0.25% hike in June. However, renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and the subsequent rise in oil prices have complicated the inflation outlook. Markets will closely monitor President Christine Lagarde's press conference for any indications on how these developments might influence future monetary policy decisions, with some analysts suggesting a potential rate hike in September.
title: ECB Expected to Hold Rates, Oil Prices Cloud Inflation Outlook
